concepts.title: Adolescence: The Bridge Between Childhood and Adulthood

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Adolescence: The Bridge Between Childhood and Adulthood' refers to.
questions.a: Adolescence is the transitional stage between childhood and adulthood, marked by rapid physical growth, hormonal change and equally deep psychological and social change. It is the stage the learner currently occupies, which is why the course opens with understanding the self at this age.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Adolescence: The Bridge Between Childhood and Adulthood'.
questions.a: A bridge stage -- body racing, identity forming, relationships renegotiated all at once.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Adolescence: The Bridge Between Childhood and Adulthood' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Personal and Social Identity of the Self

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Personal and Social Identity of the Self' refers to.
questions.a: Understanding oneself means mapping the self along two axes: personal identity -- one's abilities, interests, values and aspirations -- and social identity, the roles one plays as daughter or son, friend, student and citizen. Healthy development weaves the two into a coherent self-concept and self-esteem.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Personal and Social Identity of the Self'.
questions.a: Two mirrors form the self -- the private one of abilities and values, the social one of roles and recognition.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Personal and Social Identity of the Self' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 2.2 (source: kehe102.txt identity sections (personal identity, social identity, self concept, self esteem, roles of an adolescent))

concepts.title: Influences and Decision Making in Adolescence

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Influences and Decision Making in Adolescence' refers to.
questions.a: Adolescent choices are steered by family, peers, media and social norms -- sometimes in conflicting directions. The chapter equips learners to recognise these influences and to make reasoned decisions about studies, relationships, appearance and habits rather than drifting with pressure.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Influences and Decision Making in Adolescence'.
questions.a: Name the pressures before they name you -- decisions improve when influences are seen clearly.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Influences and Decision Making in Adolescence' taught, and from which source text?
